entries.source: Urkundenbuch des Cistercienserstiftes B. Mariae V. zu Hohenfurt in Böhmen, Nr. CLXXIV. , S. 220, CLXXIV.
entries.german:
1389. 2. Februar. Vitignabo. — Erzbischof Johann von Prag gibt den Prof essen des Klosters in Hohenfurt die Erlaubnis«, dass sie sich von jedem durch den apostolischen Stuhl bestätigten Bischof sowohl die niederen als auch die höheren Weihen ertheilen lassen können.

CLXXIV. höheren Weihen ertheilen lassen können. Johannes dei gracia archiepiscopus Pragensis apostolice sedis legatus vobis religiosis . . fratribus professis monasterii in Altouado ordinis Cisterciensis Pragensis nostre diocesis salutem in domino. Quia propter loci distanciam et viarum pericula ciuitatem Pragensem, in qua clerus sacros ordines eiusdem Pragensis diocesis recipere consueuit, comode adire non potest, ad nobilis igitur viri domini Heinrici de Rosenbergh singulares precum instancias, vt a quocum- que reuerendo ¡n Christo patre domino . . episcopo catholico per sanctam sedem apostolicam electo et confirmato canonice eiusdemque sanete sedis gratiam et sui officii executionem habente legittimam omnes sacros tam maiores quam eciam minores videlicet accolitatus subdyaconatus dyaconatus et presbyteratus ordines, prout vnicuique fratrum dicti monasterii expedicius videbitur, statutis et interuallatis a jure temporibus valeatis atque possitis canonice percipere, vobis et 207 vnicuique vestrum recipiendi et ipsis episcopis conferendi plenam tenore preseacium concedimus facultatem. Ad nostre beneplacita voluntatis presencium sub nostro sigillo testimonio litterarum. Datum in Vitignabo. Anno domini millesimo trecentesimo octoagesimo nuno die purificacionis sanete Marie die secunda mensis Februarii. Das Siegel des Erzbischofs wie in CLXIII.
entries.english: On 2 February 1389 at Vitignabo, Johann, Archbishop of Prague and legate of the Apostolic See, sends greetings in the Lord to the professed religious brothers of the Cistercian monastery of Hohenfurt in his Diocese of Prague. Because of the distance and dangers of the roads, the clergy of the diocese cannot conveniently travel to Prague, where they customarily receive sacred orders. At the special request of the noble Lord Heinrich von Rosenberg, the archbishop grants by this letter full permission for each monk to receive lawfully, at the intervals prescribed by canon law and as each monk finds appropriate, all sacred orders, both major and minor—acolyte, subdeacon, deacon, and priest—from any Catholic bishop canonically elected and confirmed by the Apostolic See who possesses its favor and legitimately exercises his office. He likewise grants such bishops full faculty to confer those orders. The archbishop's seal is as described at entry CLXIII.
